note: The last real engine codes on a generated approval. All are descriptive names the family patterns could not key on - a code like "2.4 DI-D (4N15)" reduces to "2.4" under the base-code fallback - so they are listed exactly. Applied with --only-generic.

engines.source: Mitsubishi 4N15 2.4 DI-D in the L200 and Pajero Sport, written out in full here. Same figures the Mitsubishi table gives the 4N1 family.
Mitsubishi 4D56T 2.5 in the L200 and Pajero. Same figures the Mitsubishi table gives the 4D5 family.
Toyota's 2.0 and 2.2 D-4D written as trim descriptions rather than engine codes. Same figures the Toyota table gives the AD-family.
Suzuki's bought-in diesels written descriptively - the Fiat 1.6 Multijet, the 1.3 Multijet as Z13DTJ, and the PSA DW10 as RHP. Same figures the Suzuki table gives them.
Suzuki's K14C Boosterjet written as a marketing name. Specified 0W-20, so no heavier alternative is offered.
Suzuki's older petrols - the M16A written as "1.6 VVT", the G13A, and the J15. Conventional grade suited to hot climates.
The Rover K-series 1.8 in the Minelli Tf, a Rover-based kit car. Same figures the Rover table gives it.
